A research firm surveyed $1,200$ workers who were selected at random from a large metropolitan area and asked, “Are you satisfied with the city’s public transit system?” Of those surveyed, $64%$ responded that they were satisfied.

Based on this result, which of the following statements **must** be true?

1. Of all workers in the metropolitan area, exactly $64%$ are satisfied with the public transit system.
2. If another $1,200$ workers selected at random from the area were surveyed, exactly $64%$ of them would report being satisfied.
3. If $1,200$ workers selected at random from a different metropolitan area were surveyed, $64%$ of them would report being satisfied.

A consumer group surveyed $800$ smartphone owners who were selected at random from a single city and asked, “Is your current smartphone less than two years old?” Of those surveyed, $60%$ responded “yes”.

Based on this result, which of the following conclusions are appropriate?

1. Of all smartphone owners in the city, exactly $60%$ of them have a smartphone that is less than two years old.
2. If another $800$ smartphone owners selected at random from the city were surveyed, the proportion who say “yes” is likely to be close to $60%$.
3. If $800$ smartphone owners selected at random from a different city were surveyed, the proportion who say “yes” is likely to be close to $60%$.
